faq.q: What happens to bookmarks and form fields?

faq.q: Can I merge password-protected PDFs?

faq.a: Browsers block a page from triggering many downloads at once, as a security measure. Packaging the results into one ZIP is the reliable way to hand you several files in a single action.

faq.q: Are the pages re-compressed?

faq.q: Can I split only the pages that have content?

faq.q: Can I compress a PDF that is already compressed?

faq.a: PNG is lossless, so quality settings do not apply the way they do to JPG. Convert to JPG first for photographs, or resize the dimensions, which reduces any format.

faq.q: Can I compress and resize at the same time?

faq.a: They are preserved if the output is PNG. Saving a transparent image as JPG fills transparency with a solid colour, usually white, so keep PNG when you need a transparent background.

faq.a: PNG is lossless and stores more data per pixel. A photograph that was 200 KB as JPG can easily be 2 MB as PNG. That is expected, not a fault.

faq.a: When you plan to edit and re-save repeatedly, when you need sharp text and line art, or when you need transparency. For photographs you intend to keep as photographs, JPG stays smaller.

faq.a: Yes, ideally. A non-square image is centred and padded, which can leave visible empty margins. A square source gives a clean result at every size.

faq.q: Do I need a .ico file?
faq.a: For modern browsers, no — a PNG named favicon.png linked in your HTML head is enough, and 32×32 is the common choice. .ico is only needed for very old browsers, so this tool focuses on PNG.

faq.q: Why does my icon look blurry at 16 pixels?
faq.a: Fine detail cannot survive that reduction. Simple, bold shapes read best at tab size. If your logo is intricate, consider a simplified mark specifically for the smallest sizes.

faq.q: What output size should I choose?
faq.a: Match the size you intend to display it at, times two if the screen is high density. A 64 pixel icon should be rendered at 128 or 256 to stay sharp on retina displays.

faq.q: Why does my SVG render oddly?
faq.a: Some SVGs reference external fonts or images by URL. Since this tool deliberately makes no network requests, those references cannot load. Flatten text to paths in your editor, or embed the assets, for a faithful result.

faq.q: Does it keep transparency?
faq.a: Yes, unless you choose a background colour. Leave the background unset to keep transparent areas transparent.

faq.q: Is the result as sharp as the SVG?
faq.a: At the rendered size, yes — it looks identical. Zooming in beyond that size will show pixels, because PNG is a raster format and SVG is not.

privacyNote: Base64 encoding is pure text manipulation of bytes already in memory. It needs no network connection, and your image is never transmitted to produce the string.

faq.q: What is a Base64 data URL?
faq.a: A way of writing a file as text. It begins with data: followed by the file's media type and the encoded bytes. You can paste it where an image URL would normally go in HTML or CSS.

faq.q: Should I embed large images this way?
faq.a: No. Encoding increases size by roughly a third, and the text cannot be cached separately. It suits small icons and logos; anything larger is better served as its own file.

faq.q: Will it work in a CSS background property?
faq.a: Yes. Wrap the data URL in url() as you normally would, including the quotes. That is the most common use, avoiding an extra request for a small decorative image.

faq.q: Is the output safe to share?
faq.a: Treat it exactly like the image itself. Anyone holding the string can reconstruct the picture, so it offers no protection or obfuscation.

privacyNote: The search runs entirely in memory, re-encoding the image repeatedly until it fits. No copy is ever sent anywhere; the search is your own processor doing the work.

faq.q: How does it hit an exact size?
faq.a: It encodes the image at a range of quality levels and picks the highest one that lands under your limit. That takes a few moments on a large image, because several encodings are produced and compared.

faq.q: What if it cannot reach the target?
faq.a: It reports the smallest size it could achieve and offers that file. If you need to go smaller, reduce the dimensions as well — pixel count is usually the dominant factor, more than quality.

faq.q: Will the quality suffer?
faq.a: Possibly, and the tool tells you the quality it settled on so you can judge. A modest reduction from a generous original is usually invisible; pushing far below the natural size will show artefacts.

faq.q: Why does this take longer than normal compression?
faq.a: A single compression is one encoding. This tool performs several, narrowing in on your target, so the work is a multiple of the normal case. It is still typically a second or two.

faq.a: 16, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256 pixels. Windows selects the appropriate one for each context, from a small tree-view icon up to a large thumbnail.

faq.q: Does it need to be square?
faq.a: Yes, ideally. A non-square source would be distorted, so use a square PNG. 256×256 or 512×512 is the sweet spot.

faq.q: Will transparency be preserved?

faq.q: Can I use this for a website favicon?

faq.q: How do I duplicate a page?
faq.a: List its number twice. Writing 3,3,4 gives you page three twice, then page four. There is no separate duplicate button because the order string already expresses it.

faq.q: How do I delete pages with this tool?
faq.a: Simply leave them out of the sequence. If a ten-page document gets the order 1-5,7-10, then page six is gone from the result. For a dedicated tool, use Remove PDF pages.

faq.q: Does reordering reduce quality?
faq.a: No. Pages are moved intact rather than re-rendered, so text stays selectable and images keep their original resolution.

faq.q: Can I reverse the whole document?
faq.a: Yes. Enter the range backwards — for a ten-page file, type 10-1. The tool reads a descending range as a reverse order rather than re-sorting it.

faq.q: What happens to bookmarks?
faq.a: Page content is always preserved. A bookmark tree that pointed at specific pages is not carried across, because after reordering its targets are ambiguous.

faq.q: Do the pages stay in their original order?

faq.q: Will the extracted file be smaller?

faq.q: Do the numbers show in the sidebar thumbnails?

faq.q: Why is the author field empty?
faq.a: Most PDFs simply have no author recorded. Scanners usually produce files with no metadata at all, and many export tools leave the fields blank by default.

faq.q: What does the Producer field tell me?
faq.a: It names the software that made the PDF, and often the version. Seeing Ghostscript or a word processor name here is normal; it tells you how the file was generated rather than anything about its contents.

faq.q: Can this remove the metadata?

faq.q: Is the metadata visible in a normal reader?
faq.a: Usually it is hidden behind a document-properties dialogue most people never open. It is present in the file regardless, which is why a file can reveal more than it appears to.

faq.q: Are the dates reliable?
faq.a: Treat them as hints. The creation date is set by the software that wrote the file and can be wrong, especially after a file is converted or re-saved.

privacyNote: The file is read in memory and the values are rendered on this page. Nothing is uploaded — which matters most with exactly this tool, because photos can contain your home address.

faq.q: Why does my photo show no EXIF data?
faq.a: Likely causes: it is a PNG or a screenshot (neither has an EXIF block), or it was re-saved by a platform like a social network or messaging app, which almost always strips the metadata. Photos transferred directly from a camera usually still have it.

faq.q: Is GPS really in my photos?
faq.a: Often, yes — phones record location by default when location services are on. It is one of the more surprising pieces of metadata, because the photo itself gives no visual hint that it carries your coordinates.

faq.q: Can I rely on the GPS location?
faq.a: It is as accurate as the fix the phone had when the shutter fired. Indoors or in a city centre that can be off by tens of metres, so treat it as a neighbourhood, not an address.

faq.q: What does the Orientation field mean?
faq.a: It records how the camera was held so software can rotate the image correctly. A photo that appears correctly in one app and sideways in another is usually down to this field being respected or ignored.

faq.q: How do I remove this data before sharing?
faq.a: Use the Strip EXIF metadata tool. It re-encodes the image and drops everything, including GPS.

faq.q: Does this remove GPS location?
faq.a: Yes — GPS is part of the metadata block, so it goes with everything else. The tool counts how many of your images carried coordinates so you can see what you were about to share.

faq.q: Does it reduce image quality?
faq.a: For JPEG input, slightly, because the image is re-compressed. At 92% the difference is normally invisible. Choose PNG output for a lossless result, at the cost of a larger file.

faq.q: Why is the file a different size afterwards?
faq.a: Re-encoding produces different compressed bytes, so the size shifts either way regardless of the metadata removed. With PNG output the change comes purely from the metadata being gone.

faq.q: Are the pixels changed at all?
faq.a: The pixel dimensions and visible content are identical. What changes is the encoding: the image is decoded and re-encoded rather than copied byte for byte.

faq.q: Is this different from what social media does?
faq.a: Most platforms strip metadata when you upload. The difference is that you are choosing to do it, before the file goes anywhere, rather than relying on a third party to do it after receiving everything.

privacyNote: The watermark is drawn into the image data in your browser and the file is re-encoded locally. Your unpublished work is never sent anywhere, which is the whole point of watermarking it in the first place.

faq.q: Should I use the tiled option?
faq.a: Tiling repeats the text diagonally across the image, which makes it much harder to crop out. It is the better choice for images you expect to circulate. A single corner mark is easier to read and easier to remove.

faq.q: Can a watermark be removed?
faq.a: Yes, by anyone determined enough. Cropping, painting over, or content-aware fill can all defeat it. A watermark discourages casual reuse and asserts authorship; it is not a technical protection.

faq.q: Why the shadow behind the text?
faq.a: Light text on a light background would vanish without it. A soft dark drop shadow keeps the mark legible wherever it lands, which matters when the position is fixed but the image content is not.

faq.q: Which colour should I choose?
faq.a: White with a shadow is the safest default, because it survives both dark and light areas. Black suits images that are uniformly light, such as documents.

faq.q: Can I watermark a PDF?
faq.a: Not with this tool. This one is for images; a PDF watermark is a different piece of work because it has to be drawn onto each page.
